label: hv-mol-morphogen
topic: Morphogen gradient statements: exponential decay length sqrt(D/k), scaling with size, positional-information precision bounds, and measured Bicoid / Dpp / Fgf8 numbers
summary:
Harvested 10 statements, 5 with numbers read from full text (the two Gregor 2007 Cell papers on PMC) and 5 from PubMed abstracts only. Based on articles retrieved from PubMed; DOI links are in citations.

Validation: 4 arithmetic checks against the Gregor 2007 reported values.
- FAIL: decay length = sqrt(D*tau). With lambda ~100 um and FRAP D = 0.30 um^2/s the implied lifetime is 33,333 s (9.3 h), against a gradient established in under 90 min. This is about 6x off and is the known Bicoid diffusion paradox.
- PASS: reaching lambda ~100 um in 90 min needs D of about 1.85 um^2/s; the paper says D must be far above 2.
- PASS: neighbour discrimination. Delta x / lambda = 8/100 = 8%, against the paper's ~10%.
- PASS on arithmetic, FAIL on biology: the Berg-Purcell averaging time comes out at 6,944 s against the paper's ~7,000 s, but that is nearly two hours, longer than the time available, so a single nucleus averaging over time cannot reach 10%.

Registry: none of the 10 statements is in the law registry. Grep of lean/ and tracks/lean finds morphogen only in the two Turing laws (turing-ddi, turing-wavelength). tracks/research mentions morphogens in corpus and agent files, with no decay-length law; 'decay length' / Gregor / Kicheva hit only tracks/research/agents/q1-mechanisms.json, which I did not open.

Lean: D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/hv-mol-morphogen/MorphogenGradient.lean has 5 theorems (profile slope, position-independent fold change, lifetime from length, Berg-Purcell time, scaling invariance). It reached ALL CHECKED on the second of two runs, with no sorry. The first run failed with an olean read error on a Mathlib file, not an error in my file. The captured output was cut to the last lines, so the axiom lists show for only two theorems; the counter reports 5/5 axiom lines.

Not done:
- No dataset was downloaded; the falsification tests are named but not run.
- Shh: no number harvested.
- Fgf8 and Dpp: no numeric D, k or lambda, because the abstracts carry none and I did not open the full texts.
- One neural-tube gradient-decoding paper was excluded because its abstract uses a held-out-clade species.
- Houchmandzadeh 2002 could not be located (my PMID guess was wrong).

findings.claim: S1 Exponential profile. Formal: steady state of dc/dt = D c'' - k c with a source at x=0 is c(x) = c0*exp(-x/lambda), lambda = sqrt(D/k) = sqrt(D*tau). Assumptions: 1-D, uniform D and k, steady state, linear degradation. Measured Bicoid lambda ~100 um. Registry: not present. Falsifier: FlyEx (urchin.spbcas.ru/flyex) Bcd intensity profiles; fit log c vs x, reject if residuals are systematically curved or lambda differs from sqrt(D*tau) using independently measured D and tau.
findings.evidence_quote: The observed concentration profiles have λ ~ 100 μm.
findings.confidence: high for the number (read in full text via fetch summary); FlyEx dataset named from memory, not opened

findings.claim: S2 VALIDATION (FAIL). Prediction from S1: tau = lambda^2/D. With lambda = 100 um and FRAP D = 0.30 um^2/s, tau = 10000/0.30 = 33,333 s = 9.3 h. Measured: gradient established in ~1 h (under 90 min). Predicted time is about 6x too long, so simple diffusion-degradation with the FRAP D fails. Registry: not present.
findings.value: predicted 33,333 s vs observed < 5,400 s: FAIL
findings.evidence_quote: the gradient would never reach steady-state with our measured small diffusion constant
findings.confidence: high; arithmetic is mine, inputs are the paper's reported values

findings.claim: S3 VALIDATION (PASS, consistency). Inverse of S2: to reach lambda = 100 um within t = 90 min needs D >= lambda^2/t = 10000/5400 = 1.85 um^2/s. Paper states the requirement as D much greater than 2 um^2/s, an order above the measured 0.30 +/- 0.09.
findings.evidence_quote: a cytoplasmic diffusion constant D = 0.30±0.09 μm2/s
findings.confidence: medium-high; the 'D >> 2' wording comes from the fetch tool's summary of the full text, not a verbatim quote I saw

findings.claim: S4 Competing D by FCS. Bicoid-EGFP diffusion coefficient ~7 um^2/s in cytoplasm during cycles 12-14, large enough for diffusion alone to set up the gradient. Formal: D_FCS >= lambda^2/t_establish. With S3's threshold 1.85 um^2/s, 7 > 1.85 so S1 is rescued if the FCS D is the right one. Registry: not present. Falsifier: repeat FRAP vs FCS on the same Bcd-GFP line; reject if long-range effective D stays under 2 um^2/s.
findings.evidence_quote: with a diffusion coefficient approximately 7 microm(2)/s
findings.confidence: high for the abstract value; full text not opened

findings.claim: S5 VALIDATION (PASS). Neighbour discrimination: for an exponential profile, the fractional concentration difference between nuclei Delta x apart is Delta c / c = Delta x / lambda (small Delta x). Prediction: 8 um / 100 um = 8%. Reported: ~10%. Registry: not present. Falsifier: FlyEx or Gregor-lab Bcd-GFP nuclear intensities; reject if the measured embryo-to-embryo noise at mid-embryo exceeds Delta x / lambda.
findings.value: predicted 8% vs reported ~10%: PASS (same order, within rounding of '~')
findings.evidence_quote: all of these quantities are approximately 10%
findings.confidence: high; 8 um spacing and 100 um length constant read from full text via fetch summary

findings.claim: S6 VALIDATION (arithmetic PASS, biology FAIL). Berg-Purcell limit: delta c / c ~ 1/sqrt(D*a*c*T). With D = 1 um^2/s, a = 3 nm = 0.003 um, c = 4.8 molecules/um^3 and target 0.1: T = 100/(1*0.003*4.8) = 6,944 s. Paper: about 7,000 s, nearly two hours, which exceeds the available time; so one nucleus time-averaging alone cannot reach 10%. Registry: not present. Falsifier: live hunchback transcription readouts (MS2); reject if single-nucleus readout noise reaches 10% in a window far shorter than D*a*c allows without spatial averaging.
findings.evidence_quote: approaching the limits set by basic physical principles
findings.confidence: high for inputs (full text summary); the quote is from the abstract

findings.claim: S7 Positional information in bits. Formal: I(g; x) = mutual information between gap-gene expression g and position x; reported nearly 2 bits per gene, and four gap genes give positional error sigma_x ~1% of egg length, roughly constant along the axis. Assumption: Gaussian noise approximation for the decoder. Registry: not present. Falsifier: the Dubuis/Petkova gap-gene profile data set (Princeton Gregor lab release); recompute sigma_x(x) = sqrt of inverse Fisher information, reject if above ~1 nuclear spacing (about 1.5-2% EL) over most of the axis.
findings.value: ~2 bits per gene; error ~1% egg length
findings.evidence_quote: Individual genes carry nearly two bits of information
findings.confidence: high for abstract values; the abstract text reads 'error bar of ~1' with the percent sign dropped, I read it as 1% EL; dataset location not opened

findings.claim: S8 Scaling across species. Formal: lambda / L = constant across related fly species with different egg length L, while effective D is essentially the same; under S1 this forces tau proportional to L^2 (lifetime adaptation). Registry: not present. Falsifier: Bcd profiles in species of different egg size (data in the paper's figures); regress lambda on L, reject if slope of log lambda vs log L is not near 1, or if tau does not scale as L^2.
findings.value: qualitative: D same, pattern scales with L
findings.evidence_quote: effective diffusion constants are essentially the same in closely related dipteran species
findings.confidence: medium; abstract only, no numeric lambda/L opened

findings.claim: S9 Lifetime sets length (direct test of lambda = sqrt(D*tau)). Bicoid lifetime is 50 min before cycle 14 and 15 min during cellularization; the gradient does not reach steady state; artificially shortening lifetime shortens the gradient. Formal: d lambda / d tau > 0, and under S1 lambda2/lambda1 = sqrt(tau2/tau1). Check against S2: tau = 50 min = 3000 s with lambda = 100 um implies D = lambda^2/tau = 3.3 um^2/s, between the FRAP (0.3) and FCS (7) values. Registry: not present. Falsifier: the Dronpa-Bcd perturbation series in the paper; reject if lambda ratio departs from sqrt of lifetime ratio.
findings.value: tau = 50 min then 15 min; implied D = 3.3 um^2/s (my arithmetic)
findings.evidence_quote: changing from 50 min before mitotic cycle 14 to 15 min during cellularization
findings.confidence: high for lifetimes (abstract); implied D is my calculation mixing two papers' numbers

findings.claim: S10 Other morphogens. (a) Fgf8 in zebrafish: gradient forms by free extracellular diffusion plus a receptor-endocytosis sink, so lambda = sqrt(D/k) with k set by uptake; changing uptake changes gradient shape. (b) Dpp vs Wingless in the fly wing disc: four kinetic parameters (production, effective D, degradation, immobile fraction) were measured and differ, Dpp range longer. (c) Dpp gradient scales with disc size during growth, lambda proportional to L. Registry: not present. Falsifier: Kicheva 2007 supplementary FRAP parameter table; reject if sqrt(D/k) from FRAP differs from the fitted decay length of the same discs beyond reported error.
findings.value: qualitative only; no numeric D, k, lambda in the abstracts
findings.evidence_quote: Both Dpp concentration and signaling gradients scale with tissue size during development
findings.confidence: medium; abstracts only. I did not open full texts, so I report no numeric D or lambda for Fgf8 or Dpp

findings.claim: Registry check. The law registry has no morphogen decay-length, scaling or positional-precision law. 'morphogen' appears in lean/registry only in turing-ddi and turing-wavelength (two-morphogen reaction-diffusion instability), which is a different statement. tracks/research mentions morphogens in corpus and agent files but no sqrt(D/k) law.
findings.confidence: high for lean/ and tracks/lean; tracks/research files were counted by grep, not read

findings.claim: Lean file with 5 theorems checked: profile_deriv (slope of c0*exp(-x/lam) is -(c0/lam)*exp(-x/lam)), fold_change (moving d multiplies concentration by exp(-d/lam) at any x), lifetime_from_length (lam^2 = D*tau implies tau = lam^2/D), berg_purcell_time (eps^2*D*a*c*T = 1 implies T = 1/(D*a*c*eps^2)), scaling_invariance (lam = alpha*L makes the profile at relative position s independent of L).
findings.value: ALL CHECKED on run 2 of 2; run 1 failed on an olean read error
findings.evidence_quote: ALL CHECKED: no errors, no sorryAx
findings.confidence: high; these are the algebraic/calculus skeleton only, not the full PDE steady-state uniqueness

key_claims: The textbook law lambda = sqrt(D*tau) FAILS for Bicoid with the FRAP diffusion constant: predicted 9.3 h to steady state vs under 90 min observed.
The same law is consistent if the FCS value (D ~7 um^2/s) or the measured 50 min lifetime (implied D 3.3 um^2/s) is used; the disagreement is about which D is right.
Neighbour-discrimination precision Delta x/lambda = 8% matches the reported ~10%.
Berg-Purcell averaging time recomputes to 6,944 s, matching the paper's ~7,000 s, and is too long for a single nucleus.
None of these statements is in the DELPHI law registry yet; only Turing two-morphogen laws are.
Lean file MorphogenGradient.lean: 5 theorems, ALL CHECKED, no sorry.
lay_summary: A growing embryo tells its cells where they are by using a chemical that is strong at one end and fades toward the other, like the smell of cooking fading as you walk away from the kitchen.
A simple rule says how far the chemical reaches: it depends on how fast it spreads and how long it lasts before it is broken down.
We checked that rule with real fruit-fly measurements and it failed with one way of measuring the spreading speed: the chemical would need over nine hours, but the embryo does it in about one.
Another check passed: next-door cells see about a one-tenth difference in the chemical, which is just what the fading rule predicts.
We also wrote five small maths facts about the rule and a computer proof-checker confirmed them.

glossary.morphogen: A chemical signal whose amount tells a cell where it is in the embryo.
glossary.gradient: A smooth change in amount from high at one place to low further away.
glossary.decay length (lambda): The distance over which the signal drops to about 37% of its starting value.
glossary.D (diffusion constant): How fast molecules spread out by random motion, in square micrometres per second.
glossary.k (degradation rate) and tau (lifetime): How quickly the molecule is destroyed; tau = 1/k is how long a molecule lasts on average.
glossary.steady state: When the pattern stops changing because supply and loss balance.
glossary.SDD model: Synthesis-diffusion-degradation: made at one end, spreads, and is broken down everywhere.
glossary.Bicoid (Bcd): A fruit-fly morphogen that marks the head-to-tail axis of the early embryo.
glossary.Dpp, Wingless, Fgf8, Shh: Other morphogens, in the fly wing (Dpp, Wingless), zebrafish embryo (Fgf8) and vertebrate tissues (Shh).
glossary.FRAP: Bleach a spot with a laser and time how fast fluorescence returns, to measure spreading speed.
glossary.FCS: Watch flickering of a few fluorescent molecules in a tiny spot to measure how fast they move.
glossary.Berg-Purcell limit: The best accuracy a tiny sensor can reach when counting randomly arriving molecules over a set time.
glossary.positional information: How much a cell can know about its location from the signals it reads.
glossary.bit: A unit of information; one bit is one yes/no answer.
glossary.mutual information: How much knowing one quantity reduces uncertainty about another.
glossary.scaling: The pattern keeping the same proportions when the embryo is bigger or smaller.
glossary.egg length (EL): The length of the embryo, used as the ruler for positions.
glossary.nucleus / nuclear cycle: The compartment holding DNA; early fly embryos double their nuclei in numbered rounds.
glossary.hunchback and gap genes: Genes switched on by Bicoid in broad bands along the embryo.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A computer program that checks mathematical proofs, and its library of known maths.
glossary.axiom: A starting assumption a proof is allowed to rely on.
glossary.olean: A compiled library file the Lean checker loads.

FlyEx and the Princeton gap-gene data set: named as test datasets from memory; URLs not opened or verified.

tracks/research/agents/q1-mechanisms.json has 2 hits for decay-length/author terms; I did not open it to see what it says.
The cause of the first checker failure (olean read error on a Mathlib file that exists on disk) was not diagnosed; possibly another session was using the shared build at the time.
recommendations: Register 'decay length lambda^2 = D*tau' as a law with an explicit FAIL-with-FRAP-D / PASS-with-FCS-D test record; the disagreement between the two D measurements is the scientifically interesting result.
Add the Berg-Purcell precision bound as a separate law; the Gregor 2007 inputs reproduce the paper's 7,000 s exactly and give a clean numeric test.
Next step for a real data test: pull Bcd profiles (FlyEx) and fit lambda per embryo, then test scaling lambda/L and the 10% reproducibility claim on raw data.
Open the Kicheva 2007 supplement for Dpp D and k so sqrt(D/k) can be compared with the fitted decay length; this is the cleanest direct test of S1 outside Bicoid.
Extend the Lean file with the second derivative so the steady-state equation D*c'' = k*c is proved from lam^2 = D/k, not just the slope.
